Ana (Design): quick design QA — noticed the canary allocation slider in the rollout timeline isn’t announced by NVDA/VoiceOver and the keyboard focus outline is basically invisible :grimacing: Matt (PM): thanks, can you repro steps? which browser/OS? screenshot? Ana (Design): mac+voiceover and windows+nvda, happens in chrome + ff. screenshot: https://imgur.com/a/xyz123 (timeline > version > canary allocation) Ravi (Eng): hmm, slider is implemented as a div with click handlers right now. No native input semantics. Sam (Accessibility): yep that's the problem — must be a proper role=slider with aria-valuenow/min/max and keyboard handlers. Also need an aria-live region announcing changes for screenreader users while dragging. Matt (PM): proposed microcopy: label the control "Canary allocation" and on hover show tooltip: "Fraction of traffic sent to version X" — thoughts? Ana (Design): fine with label. Can we make the visible value persistent so sighted keyboard users can see percent while moving thumb? current tooltip disappears on focus-out. Ravi (Eng): agree. Implementation sketch from my side: ```
``` Ravi (Eng): plus keyboard support (arrow keys +/-1, pageup/pagedown +/-10) and Home/End to jump. Sam (Accessibility): add `aria-valuetext` when we show percent like "10% — canary" so voice reads friendly label. Also ensure color contrast of the thumb meets 4.5:1 for focus ring. Ana (Design): I can try some visual options — maybe persistent small badge next to slider with current value, and a stronger 3px focus ring in brand-accent color with white outline for contrast. Matt (PM): one more ask — when allocation changes during an active rollout, should we log the change in the version history timeline? Curious if we should treat allocation edits as discrete events. Ravi (Eng): backend already creates a change event for allocations, but UI currently collapses minor allocation tweaks into a single entry. We could surface them as expandable deltas if the user toggles "Show minor changes". Ana (Design): yes, add a subtle divider and an "expand minor edits" affordance. That helps audits without clutter. Sam (Accessibility): also ensure that expanded deltas are keyboard-navigable and focus moves into the expanded region when opened. Matt (PM): timeline voice: "Allocation changed to 15% for version v12" — keep phrasing consistent across both toast announcements and timeline entries. Ravi (Eng): will prototype aria-live toast + history entry copy. I can have a patch for the slider semantics + keyboard by EOD tomorrow. Ana (Design): I'll mock the persistent badge + focus ring and upload a fig link in this thread. deploy-bot: deploy started for canary v12 -> v12-alpha (10% traffic) — build 2026.03.23. Matt (PM): thanks team — Sam, can you do a quick accessibility review of the mock when Ana posts it? Sam (Accessibility): 👍 will review. If all good I'll add a checklist item to the release notes: "Canary slider: ARIA semantics, keyboard support, focus visible, announced changes." Ana (Design): tagging for follow-up: @Ravi please link PR here, @Sam I'll ping you once mocks posted. Quick wins first: role=slider + aria-valuenow + keyboard handlers. Ravi (Eng): noted. I'll drop a link when the branch is up: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/???? Matt (PM): moving to the next design sync agenda: timeline compact mode and keyboard scrubbing — but separate thread. For this one, good plan. :thumbsup:
